sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri Jai Prakash Kushwah - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Dinesh Savita - Public Prosecutor for respondent/
 Order

This is first anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C/482 of BNSS filed by the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.429/2025, registered at Police Station- Kotwali, District Bhind for the offence punishable under Sections 316(2) of BNS.

2. Prosecution story in short is that Mata Prasad Yadav submitted a written application to Police Station City Kotwali, Bhind, stating that the applicant/accused and other persons Harisingh,
Havildar Yadav and the informant, are relatives.

Against Havildar Yadav, Harisingh, Crime No.
63/2024 under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 304-B of IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, which is pending before the Court.

In January 2026, the applicant/accused came to the informant Mata Prasad and said that he would get the case between Harisingh and Havildar compromised and that they would turn hostile in their testimony, for which an amount of rupees NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24585 2 MCRC-43890-2025 fifty lacs would have to be paid.
The informant conveyed this matter to Havildar Singh, who agreed and told him to pay the money in the presence of witnesses.
The applicant/accused agreed to receive rupees fifty lacs.

On 03.02.2025, a sum of rupees sixteen lacs was transferred via RTGS from Account No. 30077091383 belonging to Devendra, son of Havildar into the account of the applicant/accused Akshay Kumar,
Account No.4486000100092448.

On 04.02.2025, in front of the house of Shrinath Sharma,
resident of Ater Road, Bhind, in the presence of witnesses Shivraj, Rajeswar, Shivnarayan, Ramveer and Vivek, the applicant was given rupees thirty four lacs in cash.
The applicant took the aforesaid money but did not effect any compromise.
When asked, he stated that he had given the said money to Hari Singh Yadav and if the compromise did not take place, he would return the money.

However,
he neither returned the money nor got the compromise executed.

Learned counsel for the applicant contended that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this matter as he is a prime prosecution witness in Crime No. 63/2024 related with dowry death of late Smt. Kalpana, who was sister-in-law (bhabhi) of the applicant.
The in-laws of the deceased, against whom the said case is pending, have been continuously pressurizing the applicant and the parents of the deceased to enter into a compromise.
Upon refusal, a false case has been engineered against the applicant through the informant.
Thus, the FIR is nothing but a counter blast.

The financial transactions and bank records are already in the custody of the investigating a g e n c y , t h e r e f o r e , c u s t o d i a l i n t e r r o g a t i o n o f t h e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-GWL:24585 3 MCRC-43890-2025 applicant is not required.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents.
He undertakes to fully cooperate with the investigation and trial and will not tamper with the prosecution witnesses in any manner.
Hence, he prays that the applicant be released on anticipatory bail.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the application.

5. Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

Considering the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is hereby directed that in the event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of Investigating Officer/Investigating Agency.\
7.

3. The applicant will not indulge himself in extending inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the Police Officer, as the case may be.
4. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24585 4 MCRC-43890-2025 offence of which he is accused;

5. The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial;
6.

benefit of bail shall immediately be withdrawn.
8. The present application stands allowed and disposed of.
9. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
10. Certified copy as per rules.
